classes.name_en: President, direct, with a deputy president as running mate
classes.locator: https://www.parliament.go.ke/sites/default/files/2023-03/The_Constitution_of_Kenya_2010.pdf (Art. 138(4): more than half of all the votes cast and at least 25% in each of more than half of the counties, else a fresh election between the top two within 30 days)
classes.note: Under the independence constitution as amended, the president was declared elected unopposed with each general election from 1969 to 1988; the first contested presidential poll followed the return to multiparty politics on 29 December 1992. Under the former constitution a winner also needed 25% in at least five of the eight provinces. The Supreme Court annulled the 8 August 2017 result and IEBC held a fresh presidential election on 26 October 2017. Kenyans abroad vote only for President and in referendums.

classes.locator: https://www.parliament.go.ke/sites/default/files/2023-03/The_Constitution_of_Kenya_2010.pdf (Art. 97(1)(a): "two hundred and ninety members, each elected by the registered voters of single member constituencies")
classes.note: First past the post in single-member constituencies: 117 in 1963, 158 from 1966 (when the Senate merged into the House), 188 from 1986, 210 from 1996, and 290 from 2013 (IIBRC report s. 2.1.2; Constitution Art. 89). classes.name: Kura ya maamuzi (constitutional referendum)
classes.name_en: National constitutional referendums
classes.locator: https://www.parliament.go.ke/sites/default/files/2023-03/The_Constitution_of_Kenya_2010.pdf (Art. 255(1)-(2): amendments touching the listed matters need approval by referendum; Arts. 256-257 for parliamentary and popular initiatives)
classes.note: Two held: 21 November 2005 (the proposed new constitution, rejected 57% to 43%, run by the former Electoral Commission of Kenya) and 4 August 2010 (the present constitution, approved; run by the IIEC). The Punguza Mizigo (2019) and Building Bridges (2020) popular initiatives reached IEBC's signature verification, but neither went to a vote (BBI was struck down by the courts).

classes.name: Recall elections of members of Parliament and county assemblies
classes.name_en: Recall elections
classes.locator: https://www.iebc.or.ke/uploads/resources/G16qxyy4rA.pdf (ss. 45-48: petition by 30% of voters after a High Court finding; yes/no recall election valid if at least half the registered voters concur)
classes.note: Constitution Art. 104 gives the right to recall members of Parliament; County Governments Act s. 27 gives wards the right to recall their member of county assembly (IEBC's administrative procedures). No recall election has been held.
classes.disposition_reason: No recall election has ever been held under ss. 45-48 of the Elections Act or s. 27 of the County Governments Act; the class stays recorded so one would be classified when held.

classes.name: Party-list nominations (Article 90)
classes.name_en: Nominated members of the National Assembly, Senate, and county assemblies
classes.locator: https://www.parliament.go.ke/sites/default/files/2023-03/The_Constitution_of_Kenya_2010.pdf (Art. 90 and Arts. 97(1)(c), 98(1)(b)-(d), 177(1)(b)-(c): seats allocated to parties in proportion to the seats they won)
classes.disposition_reason: No vote is cast for these seats: IEBC allocates them from each party's share of elected seats under Art. 90 and gazettes the nominees; the allocation follows from the elected-seat results.

classes.name: Party nominations
classes.name_en: Party primaries and nominations
classes.locator: https://www.iebc.or.ke/uploads/resources/G16qxyy4rA.pdf (ss. 13 and 27: parties nominate under their own rules, submitted to the Commission)
classes.disposition_reason: Parties run their own nominations under s. 13 of the Elections Act and the Political Parties Act; IEBC only receives the rules and the nominees, and publishes no primary returns.

classes.name: Speakers of Parliament and county assemblies
classes.name_en: Speakers elected by the houses and county assemblies
classes.locator: https://www.iebc.or.ke/uploads/resources/G16qxyy4rA.pdf (s. 21 and First Schedule: election of speaker of county assembly by its members)
classes.disposition_reason: Speakers are elected by the members of each house or county assembly (Constitution Arts. 106 and 178), not by voters, and no public returns are published.

classes.name: Mayors and council chairmen (to 2013)
classes.name_en: Mayors and chairmen of local authorities, chosen by councillors

classes.disposition_reason: Councillors chose their mayors and chairmen; no popular vote and no public returns.

classes.name: Judges
classes.name_en: Judicial offices
classes.locator: https://www.parliament.go.ke/sites/default/files/2023-03/The_Constitution_of_Kenya_2010.pdf (Art. 166(1): the President appoints the Chief Justice, the Deputy Chief Justice, and all other judges on the recommendation of the Judicial Service Commission)
classes.disposition_reason: Kenya elects no judges; all are appointed under Art. 166.
